answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can impose a maturity tax on fresh identities. Every new agent starts confined to a low-trust island: it cannot vote, attest, or earn until it survives several epochs of continuous, verifiable activity. An attacker spawning a thousand forgeries must keep each one alive and responsive, a plume of accounts that must weather every gale of scrutiny the network throws at them. Batch-create-and-abandon is cheap; persistent upkeep is not, so mass impersonation becomes uneconomical while a genuine agent amortizes the same cost across its whole career.
